Officials reported a surge in automated bot traffic over several days, temporarily knocking portions of the website offline, including election-related pages used by voters to locate ballot drop boxes. The affected pages have since been restored, although investigators have not confirmed whether the bot traffic was directly connected to the cyberattack. Hobbs emphasized that the state's vote-counting machines were not affected, as county tabulation systems are not connected to the internet. The incident remains under investigation, with no confirmed attribution or evidence that votes were altered. 🚨 A PackageKit race condition can let a local unprivileged user gain root access on affected Linux systems; CVE-2026-41651 PoC: https:// github.com/0xBlackash/CVE-2026 -41651 The flaw is a time-of-check time-of-use race condition in PackageKit transaction flags. An attacker with local access can abuse the transaction state to install arbitrary packages as root, including packages containing privileged install scripts. PackageKit | Local Privilege Escalation CVSS: 8.8 High Affected: PackageKit 1.0.2 through 1.3.4 Fixed: PackageKit 1.3.5 Impact: Local privilege escalation to root The vulnerability, dubbed Pack2TheRoot, affects multiple Linux distributions and can be exploited by a local low-privileged user without additional user interaction.

🚨 A Samba printing flaw can turn a malicious print job name into remote code execution; CVE-2026-4480 PoC: https:// github.com/0xBlackash/CVE-2026 -4480 The vulnerability affects Samba’s printing subsystem when %J is used inside a custom print command. A client-controlled print job name can reach the shell without proper escaping, allowing shell metacharacters to alter the command being executed. Samba Printing | Command Injection RCE CVSS: 9.8 Critical Affected: Samba < 4.22.10, < 4.23.8, and < 4.24.3 Fixed: Samba 4.22.10, 4.23.8, and 4.24.3 Impact: Unauthenticated remote code execution under affected configurations The repository documents the vulnerable configuration, attack path, affected versions, detection guidance, and mitigation steps.

🚨 A filename overflow in the D-Link DIR-505 TFTP upload path can be chained into unauthenticated remote code execution as root PoC: https:// github.com/Walnut1337/DIR-505_ filename_rce The issue affects the DIR-505 A1 running firmware 1.10B02. An attacker-controlled TFTP filename is copied into fixed-size stack buffers, allowing control of the return address and execution of a ROP chain that ultimately calls system(). D-Link DIR-505 | Pre-auth RCE CVSS: 9.8 Critical Affected: DIR-505 A1 firmware 1.10B02 Impact: Unauthenticated remote code execution as root Status: Verified end-to-end against emulated real firmware The repository includes the full exploit chain, ROP layout analysis, a TFTP client, proof of root-shell execution, and remediation guidance.

The intrusion began in August 2026 and remained undetected until October 23, when DreamHost discovered attackers had exploited a vulnerability in its web-based File Manager. The attackers obtained FTP/SFTP usernames and passwords, along with webmail credentials and session tokens. In some cases, the stolen credentials may have allowed hackers to access customer inboxes and read private emails. DreamHost | Security Incident • Attack period: August to October 23, 2026 • Affected accounts: Well under 10% • Exposed: FTP/SFTP credentials and webmail login information • Impact: Potential unauthorized access to customer email accounts • Vulnerability: Undisclosed File Manager security flaw • Investigation: Ongoing DreamHost says it has blocked the attackers, patched the vulnerability, and reset affected credentials. The company found no evidence that customer billing information or control panel credentials were compromised. The exact number of affected customers remains undisclosed. 🚨🇫🇷 French Banking Giant Crédit Mutuel Arkéa Confirms Cyberattack, Hackers Suspected of Stealing $133 Million French banking group Crédit Mutuel Arkéa has confirmed a sophisticated cyberattack after hackers allegedly stole more than $133 million by compromising one of the bank's third-party service providers. According to the bank, attackers gained access through a supplier's platform and used Arkéa's own account to transfer funds to other financial institutions. Some of the stolen money was potentially converted into cryptocurrency through specialized exchanges. Blockchain investigator @ZachXBT first reported the incident, tracing suspicious withdrawals and transactions believed to be connected to laundering the stolen funds. Arkéa acknowledged that the estimated $133 million loss was broadly consistent with its findings but said the final amount remains under investigation. The bank confirmed that some assets have already been frozen and recovery efforts are underway. Customer accounts were not compromised, and the institution says the incident has been contained without affecting customer funds or its financial stability. French authorities are investigating how the attackers gained access and carried out the transfers. Source: https:// therecord.media/french-bank-co nfirms-cyber-heist Zach's Telegram Post: https:// t.me/investigations/375

French authorities are investigating the intrusion, while EFS confirms that blood collection and distribution services remain operational.
